evals.expected: A strong answer recalls at least one GENUINELY structural analog and maps it relation-by-relation, not by keyword. The canonical strong analog is weighted fair queuing / max-min fairness for shared network bandwidth (or its cousins: CPU fair-share scheduling like CFS, or hierarchical token-bucket / HTB traffic shaping). The relational mapping must line up: drivers↔link bandwidth/CPU time-slices; micro-warehouses↔competing flows/processes; orders↔packets/jobs; the 300-driver pool↔fixed link capacity; the 30-min deadline↔packet deadline/latency bound; 'pull more than fair share when others idle'↔work-conserving max-min fairness (spare capacity redistributed to active flows); 'no warehouse can starve others'↔per-flow guaranteed minimum / weighted shares. A strong answer EXPLICITLY FLAGS where the analog only partially transfers — the disanalogies are the discriminator: (1) PERISHABILITY + travel/route time — a reassigned driver isn't instantly available like a freed time-slice; there is a non-preemptible commitment (a driver mid-route can't be yanked) and a repositioning cost, which pure WFQ ignores; (2) the deadline makes it a real-time/admission-control problem, so graceful degradation (d) requires DROPPING/admission decisions (refund-minimizing triage: shed orders that can't make the 30-min cutoff rather than spreading everyone thin) — analogous to AQM/deadline-aware dropping, not just sharing; (3) lumpy indivisible 'quanta' (a driver ≈ several orders over an hour) vs near-continuous bandwidth, so fairness is coarse-grained. Concrete mechanism expected: a max-min / weighted-fair allocator computing each warehouse's guaranteed floor from a backlog- or arrival-weighted share of 300, then redistributing unused capacity to backlogged sites each short reassignment cycle (e.g. every 30-60s); state kept = per-warehouse open-order backlog/age, committed drivers, projected free-up times; assignment = give next free driver to the most under-served backlogged warehouse (largest deadline-risk-weighted deficit); reclaim = a driver returns to the pool on route completion (with optional pre-emption only of not-yet-started picks). Failure modes the answer should name: thrashing/repositioning churn if it reassigns too aggressively, starvation of steady low-volume sites if weights track raw volume instead of guaranteeing a floor, deadline cliff under sustained overload, and staleness of the central state between cycles. Weak/penalizable answers exhibit the pattern's failure modes: a FORCED or SURFACE analog (e.g. 'it's like a restaurant waitlist' or 'load balancing servers' invoked by keyword with no element-by-element mapping); a MAPPING BREAK where they map drivers↔bandwidth but then silently ignore perishability, travel time, and the deadline and just describe vanilla round-robin or static per-site quotas; or OVER-CONFIDENCE TRANSFER — asserting WFQ/token-bucket 'solves it' wholesale without flagging that preemption, perishability, and admission/dropping don't come along for free. Failing to address requirement (c) graceful degradation as an admission/triage problem (vs naive even-spreading) is a completeness gap.
evals.format_spec: Prose-shaped, structured in two clearly separated stages: (1) an 'analogs' stage with one labeled block per recalled analog, each containing the analogous problem, its known solution, and an explicit element-by-element structural mapping that flags where it breaks down; followed by (2) a 'solution' stage that builds the allocation scheme FROM the mapping(s) and covers all of (a)-(d) plus algorithm, state kept, assign/reclaim mechanics, and named failure modes. The analog stage must precede and visibly inform the solution — analogs presented as decoration after an independently-derived answer do not satisfy the format. No rigid JSON/table required (analogical exploration is prose-shaped), but the two stages must be distinguishable and the mapping must be enumerated, not gestured at.
evals.tone: Senior systems/operations engineer thinking aloud to a peer — analytical, precise, intellectually honest about where an analogy stops holding. Confident but not glib; willing to say 'this part transfers, this part does not.' Technical vocabulary appropriate for an engineer, no hand-waving and no salesy certainty.
